title: Chuunibyou Research
paragraphs: “Rifana, Raphtalia—wait up!”
Kou seems to have taken a particular liking to big sister and her friends, even more than Sakura.
“Okay, okay. This way!”
“Yeah! Hug both of you!”
Kou hugs big sister and her friend.
“Where should we go today? Follow Sadina and go swimming?”
“What should we do, Raphtalia-chan?”
“Hmm…”
“Or cooking? I love Raphtalia’s cooking just like I love Iwatani’s!”
Kou looks at big sister with sparkling eyes. Big sister strokes Kou’s head with a wry smile.
“I want to study magic. The other day, I lost to Rifana in an illusion magic duel.”
“It depends on how you do it, but… Raphtalia-chan, when you use magic or infuse power, the flow of energy is kind of unique, so you’re not great at seeing through things.”
“Kou, got dizzy!”

If I recall correctly, big sister specializes in light and dark illusion magic. Even the royal court magicians confirmed this after examining her. Her friend is also skilled in illusion magic, but hers stems from fire.

Would that be like a mirage? They have similar but fundamentally different natures… Father mentioned that both of them excel in deception magic. Kou willingly volunteers to be their test subject for magic practice. Apparently, the illusions they show him are fun to watch.

Maybe I should ask them to show me sometime? Even if it’s just an illusion, I’d like to see them recreate Filo-tan so I can meet her again. While they’re having such a fun discussion, I wave to them and continue observing the village.
…Oh? In the shadow of a building, away from prying eyes, I catch a glimpse of Ren and what looks like Kuro-chan. I quietly sneak closer to get a better look.
“Sha-keen! Do it like this!”
Kuro-chan covers his right eye with his hand, raises his elbow, and strikes a pose like a hero from a sentai show.
Is he showing off his cool poses to Ren?
“No, doing it this way looks cooler.”
Ren covers his right eye the same way but spreads his fingers and gives a sidelong glance, striking a pose while looking at Kuro-chan. Ren seems to be surprisingly into it too.
“Cool! Like this?”
Kuro-chan practices the pose Ren taught him, adding his own little twists.
“And then… if Ren wore cool armor and added a mask, it’d be perfect, right? Either gold or red would be good.”
Ren crossed his arms and let out a smug laugh.

“Too naive. We’re going for a dark theme. Sure, black and gold have a sense of luxury, but that’s off the mark. The right colors are definitely black or blue. We’re not some boring heroes of justice! Don’t get it wrong!”
“Got it! So, it’s an all-black, dark theme! Then the mask is black too, and the cape is black… should Kuro use a sword like Sakura?”
Wouldn’t that make it all pitch black? Well, Sakura-chan looks cool using dual blades, whether in her Filolial form or her angelic form.
“Sakura’s style is cool because she fights like she’s dancing. But you shouldn’t just copy her. Copying is lame.”
“Hmm… then what should I do?”
“Weapons aren’t everything. You can still look cool by leaping high, like a feather drifting down, and then landing a kick!”
“Like Yuki?”
“That guy used to control feathers remotely. I’m not a fan of floating weapons, though.”
Ren and Kuro-chan were having quite a deep discussion.
“They look like they’re having a lot of fun.”
When I turned around, Father was behind me, watching Ren and Kuro with amusement.
“Indeed. But didn’t Ren find it hard to keep up with Kuro-chan’s enthusiasm?”
“You already know Ren likes this kind of stuff. He’s into the cool and dark vibe.”
“Should I join in and strike a pose? It looks kind of fun.”
I was about to take a step forward and call out to them. But Father grabbed my hand and stopped me.
“Wait, wait. Ren’s only playing along because he’s keeping it a secret. If they notice we’re watching, it’ll be a disaster.”
“Is that so?”
“Definitely. It won’t end well. Pretending not to notice is the kindest thing we can do.”
What a complicated situation. Kuro-chan is openly trying to look cool, but Ren seems to think it’s embarrassing.
“By the way… Motoyasu-kun, didn’t you make a secret base when you were a kid?”
“I did. With the pigs.”

I don’t remember much from my early elementary school days, but when I reunited with a pig I knew as a child during high school, the memories started coming back. That childhood romance with a pig… for me, it’s nothing but a dark chapter of my past.
“…It’s a little different from the secret bases I know, but… those kinds of things are all about enjoying the fantasy.”
“I see… I understand.”

Even though the essence is the same, I wonder where the big difference comes from… Oh, now that I think about it, there was a time when I thought heavy metal and punk were cool. Even though I couldn’t drink it, I used to pretend to be an adult by drinking coffee. I also thought being able to play instruments or stylishly enjoying sports was cool at some point. It’s probably that same phase of wanting to be cool. Well, in any case, I learned most of those things from the pigs. As I was observing this nostalgic scene, Itsuki approached us and looked at Ren and Kuro-chan.
“What are they doing?”
“Probably brainstorming their middle school dark fantasy settings. They both seem to like the dark theme. Wouldn’t you be able to join in, Itsuki?”
“Please don’t. I have no interest in joining them.”
Itsuki refused flatly.
Oh? He’s unusually reserved.
“I think you’d fit right in, unlike Motoyasu-kun.”
“…Should I question why you think that?”
“Hm? Perfect—”
“Alright, I get it. Just stop.”
Before Father could finish his sentence, Itsuki gave up. That was quick.
“Hidden justice, dark themes… it’s the same category. In a different situation, it wouldn’t be so bad.”
“Father did call Itsuki the vice-general.”
“That’s the angle… well, that’s still kind of a hero route, so I think Itsuki would fit right in.”
“Well… I can’t deny that. But I don’t want to be seen as part of the same crowd. I’d probably say something like, ‘I’m different from everyone else.’”
“Don’t go too hard on the self-deprecation.”
As we were chatting, at some point, Keel had slipped into Ren and Kuro-chan’s circle. It seems Keel isn’t someone Ren feels embarrassed around.
“If you let your cape flutter and laugh loudly, it’s cooler!”
“That’s what villains do! It’s cooler to calmly explain how strong you are!”
Kuro-chan and Keel’s eyes sparkled with excitement. It’s nice to see them getting along so well. But Itsuki looked exasperated by Ren’s words.
“I’m not sure how I feel about this… I get that Ren-san is indulging his inner child.”
“Isn’t it that Ren is the kind of guy younger boys look up to?”
“That might be true. Anyway, shouldn’t we leave before they notice us?”

And so, we quietly slipped away from the lively meeting between Kuro-chan and Ren. After that, a messenger from Trash came and proposed hiring a combat advisor. Apparently, a letter had already been sent to someone suitable for the role, so all that was left was for us to go.

We headed to the site, but… what was the deal with them being bedridden? In the end, one dose of Yggdrasil medicine cured them instantly. By the way, this old woman was someone Father had treated in the first world and even the one before that. Well, with that, the combat advisor was secured.
